section.sectionSummaryBrief: Oil's concealment is higher than that of water, as oil is unfit for drinking entirely, representing a concealment beyond revelation.
section.t: that this matter of the concealment of oil
is more elevated even than the concealment of water, which has no taste
it is even possible to derive pleasure from it
(except that in order to derive pleasure from it, a person must have a sensation of lack
is not only something from which one cannot derive pleasure, but it is entirely unfit for drinking,
because it is a level of concealment that is above revelation.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The distinction between wine, water, and oil corresponds to their spiritual levels: wine is Binah, water is Chochmah, and oil is Chochmah S timaah, which is above revelation.
section.t: that this distinction between wine, water, and oil
and oil is unfit for drinking]
and therefore it has no taste,
but nevertheless it is fit for drinking, and even one can derive pleasure from it,
and oil is Chochmah S timaah, which is above the revelation of Binah and also above the revelation of Chochmah,

section.sectionSummaryBrief: The altar's dedication was through anointing with oil, representing Chochmah S timaah, and the addition of spices in the anointing oil alludes to the level of smell, which is even higher than oil and relates to Torah's hidden essence that nevertheless issues in practical law.
section.t: And this is that the dedication of the altar was by anointing it with the anointing oil,
for by drawing into it from the aspect of Chochmah S timaah
through this there was also drawn the power for the burning of the offerings and for the libation of wine of Binah and the libation of water of Chochmah48.
that in the anointing oil there were spices49,
which is even higher than oil.
And the explanation of this may be said,
although it is above taste and human pleasure, to the point that it is unfit for drinking,
But smell is not grasped by touch,
a thing from which the soul derives pleasure, not the body51.
And from this one may also understand regarding the levels of the wisdom of Torah, which are compared to oil and to smell,
that the Torah being compared to oil refers, as above, to the secrets of secrets,
to the point that they are clothed in letters.
But the matter of smell in Torah is entirely above comprehension.
although it is a thing from which the soul derives pleasure and not the body,
that through a strong smell one restores the soul that has been drawn into revelation in the body,
similarly it may be said regarding the matter of smell in Torah,
that it is drawn into actual practical ruling,
to the point that Moshiach will "smell and judge"53,
for the aspect of smell in him will be drawn into actual practical ruling
except that the reason for the ruling is entirely above intellect.
And it may be said that this is like "Shav was silent"54
for although this was for him a level of vision of Chochmah that was not revealed in intellect at all,
he issued an actual practical ruling.
